S1-rank: injective priorities: rank(v) = position of v in V sorted by (Ω(v), v); p'(v) = 2·rank(v) + (Ω(v) mod 2).
S1-val: valuation of v under (σ, σ̄): (c, P, ℓ), c = the most relevant (max p') vertex of the cycle the play from v ends in, P = set of vertices on the play before reaching c with p' > p'(c), ℓ = number of steps to reach c.
S1-ord: order (better for Even): compare reward of c (p'(c) if even, −p'(c) if odd); then P by the signed weight Σ_{u∈P} (+2^rank(u) if Ω(u) even else −2^rank(u)); then ℓ: if c is odd, longer is better for Even; if c even, shorter is better.
S1-xi: Ξσ = valuation of every vertex under σ and Odd's OPTIMAL counterstrategy σ̄ (minimising this order at every vertex at once).
S1-dual: Odd's side: everything on the DUAL game G^d (owner swapped, Ω + 1); τ is an "Even" strategy of G^d; Ξτ, τ̄ (= Even's optimal counterstrategy to τ, as a G^d-Odd strategy), Iτ computed there.
S2: S2 Improving edges: Iσ = {(v, w) : owner(v) = Even, w ≠ σ(v), Ξσ(w) strictly better than Ξσ(σ(v))}; Iτ the same on G^d for τ.
S4: S4 Iteration (one iteration = one pass with Iσ ∪ Iτ ≠ ∅; both steps computed from the SAME (σ, τ), applied together):
S4a: a. If Iσ ≠ ∅: A(v) = {σ(v)} ∪ {w : (v, w) ∈ Iσ} for Even v. Arena H: Even v keeps only edges to A(v); Odd v keeps only the edge to τ(v). σ_new = Odd's optimal counterstrategy (S1 procedure) in the dual of H to the dual-Even strategy τ, read as an Even strategy of G. (Even's one-player optimum against τ among "keep or take an improving edge".) Else σ_new = σ.
S4b: b. If Iτ ≠ ∅: A(v) = {τ(v)} ∪ {w : (v, w) ∈ Iτ} for Odd v. Arena H': Odd v keeps only edges to A(v); Even v only the edge to σ(v). τ_new = Odd's optimal counterstrategy (S1 procedure on H', not dual) to σ. Else τ_new = τ.
S4c: c. FALLBACK, if σ_new = σ and τ_new = τ: if Iσ ≠ ∅, for every Even v with an improving edge set σ_new(v) = the w with (v, w) ∈ Iσ maximising (Ξσ(w), w) (best valuation, ties: larger index); otherwise do the same for Odd on Iτ with G^d's valuations. Count it.

NT: (T-2) **Claim NT (no tie on a 1-sink game; mine).** Let G with ι be a 1-sink game in [F11] §5's sense, with sink x, and σ a player-0 strategy with Ξ_ι ⊴ Ξ_σ. Then Ξ_σ(u) ≠ Ξ_σ(u′) for all nodes u ≠ u′. Proof. By Sink Seeking (p. 8) every Ξ_σ(u) has cycle component x; every other node is more relevant than x (Sink Existence), so the cycle is x's loop and the path component of Ξ_σ(u) is the set of ALL nodes of the play from u before x, u itself included (the paper's own remark, p. 8: «the path-length component equals the cardinality of the path component»). Ξ_σ(x) = (x, ∅, 0) differs from every other value. If u, u′ ≠ x had equal values, u′ would lie on u's play and u on u′'s play; plays are positional, so u's play would return to u before reaching x: a cycle without x, against Sink Seeking. ∎
